canonical_subtitle: One Schmidt-spectrum path, many entanglement metrics.

terms.definition: A time-ordered projection of a declared Schmidt-spectrum path, usually using largest Schmidt value and one spectrum functional.
Time evolution of the ordered reduced-density-matrix eigenvalues for a declared pure-state bipartition.
The family of trajectory projections obtained from several declared spectrum functionals on one Schmidt-spectrum path.
Coarse trajectory morphology that remains recognizable under replacement of one declared Schmidt-spectrum metric by another.
terms.historical_label: quoted “topological invariant” of an entanglement trajectory

terms.definition: Opposite scalar changes among valid metric classes on a transition not ordered by majorization.
The finite-dimensional feasible interval of a declared spectrum functional conditioned on the largest Schmidt value, bounded by concentrated and equal-tail spectra.
Explaining several scalar measures as nonlinear observations of one Schmidt spectrum without requiring universal agreement.
A finite-Haar, Wishart, Marchenko-Pastur, spectral-edge, or bulk-correlation benchmark used after exact spectrum geometry is fixed.

preferred_search_phrases: exact entropy boundary largest Schmidt eigenvalue
